data.text:
Korean refiners will be forced to slash run rates by 20–40% from April. The war-driven supply shock may be unavoidable. The government response, however, is entirely self-inflicted.

At the onset of the crisis, the president was busy touring Singapore and the Philippines, showing zero sense of urgency. The administration delivered nothing that could remotely qualify as a response.

If anyone still believes diplomatic photo-ops matter more than energy security in the middle of a supply crisis, they have no understanding of how the real world works.

And after all that, the solution was an outdated fuel price cap. A policy straight out of a different era. The industry minister repeating “diversify crude imports” adds nothing when physical flows are already constrained.

The recent semiconductor boom and the irrational equity rally clearly gave people the wrong idea about Korea’s fundamentals. Strip away the noise, and the level of crisis management is exactly what you would expect.
